title: Achieve at least 20% mean weight loss with an approved incretin treatment

concept.text: Produce substantial, sustained weight reduction during pharmacological treatment of obesity. Semaglutide established roughly 15% mean loss, and tirzepatide achieved 20.9% at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-1. Proposed completion test: FDA chronic weight-management approval supported by a randomized phase 3 trial demonstrating at least 20% mean baseline weight reduction at approximately 72 weeks in adults without diabetes, with superiority to placebo under an estimand that includes treatment discontinuation. Test set by: FDA sets approval; SURMOUNT-1 investigators prespecified the trial endpoints and estimands. The 20% boundary is an editorial breakthrough threshold, not an FDA approval requirement. Reported achieved: FDA approved tirzepatide (Zepbound) on 8 November 2023, following SURMOUNT-1; semaglutide (Wegovy) received chronic weight-management approval on 4 June 2021. Overlaps: END-05. Sources given: [FDA Wegovy approval announcement](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFDA/bulletins/2e2adc7) ; [FDA Zepbound approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-new-medication-chronic-weight-management) ; [SURMOUNT-1 primary publication](https://www.darmzentrum-bern.ch/fileadmin/darmzentrum/Education/Journal_Club/2022/JC-22-07-20_NEJM_Tirzepatide_Once_Weekly_for_the_Treatment.pdf).

page.title: Incretin treatment producing at least 20% mean weight loss
page.definition: An FDA-approved incretin receptor agonist—a drug activating receptors for gut hormones—produces at least 20% mean weight loss at 72 weeks in adults without diabetes who have obesity, or overweight with a weight-related complication. The analysis includes participants who discontinue treatment.

goal.need: In 2024, 16% of adults worldwide were living with obesity. FDA associates loss of 5–10% of body weight through diet and exercise with reduced cardiovascular risk in adults with obesity or overweight.

figures.caption: Global adults aged 18 years or older, 2024
figures.note: The obesity population is included in the overweight population.

statements.quote: In light of increasing rates of both obesity and overweight in the United States, today’s approval addresses an unmet medical need.
statements.context: FDA's announcement of Zepbound approval on 8 November 2023.

statements.body: European Association for the Study of Obesity, Obesity Management Task Force
statements.quote: A greater (20% or more) weight loss may be considered for those with greater degrees of obesity
statements.context: The passage specifies BMI ≥35 kg/m². BMI is weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. This is an individual treatment objective without a specified drug or population mean.

completion.title: An approved incretin treatment produces at least 20% mean weight loss at 72 weeks.
completion.criterion: An incretin receptor agonist receives FDA approval for chronic weight management, supported by a randomized phase 3 trial in adults without diabetes showing a point estimate of ≥20% mean baseline weight reduction at 72 weeks and superiority to placebo under an analysis including treatment discontinuation. Achieved by tirzepatide: SURMOUNT-1 randomized 2,539 adults; 15 mg weekly produced 20.9% mean loss (95% CI 19.9–21.8), versus 3.1% with placebo, P<0.001. FDA approved Zepbound on 8 November 2023.
completion.set_by: Atlas-defined composite of FDA approval and SURMOUNT-1 efficacy evidence; no outside body identified sets the combined test.
completion.basis: FDA's 2025 draft guidance, EMA's 2007 guideline, EASO's treatment goals and SURMOUNT-1's endpoints were searched; none defines this approval-linked threshold of ≥20% mean loss. EASO's ≥20% objective concerns individual patients with BMI ≥35 kg/m²; SURMOUNT-1's ≥20% endpoint concerns responder proportions. The completion test combines approval with the trial population, duration and analysis supporting the reported mean.

milestones.title: An incretin agonist reduces body weight in obese mice versus vehicle at P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: The published laboratory test compares body weight during chronic treatment of diet-induced obese mice with vehicle, using repeated-measures ANOVA and P<0.05. Coskun et al. reported that tirzepatide passed this test and produced greater weight loss than semaglutide. Starting mouse weight was about 45 g; group sizes were not stated in the accessible main text.
milestones.set_by: Coskun et al., Eli Lilly and collaborators, published preclinical experiment, Figure 3; an experiment-specific test.
milestones.threshold_quote: P < 0.05 using one-way ANOVA repeated measures versus the vehicle

milestones.title: An incretin agonist reduces human body weight versus placebo by day 29 at P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: The phase 1b test compares change in body weight with placebo at day 29, using a mixed model and a 5% significance level. Among 53 participants with type 2 diabetes, tirzepatide titrated to 10 mg produced a placebo-adjusted reduction of 2.62 kg (95% CI 1.45–3.79). Body weight was a secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly's phase 1b proof-of-concept study, reported by Coskun et al., clinical outcomes and Figure 5; written for adults with type 2 diabetes.
milestones.threshold_quote: Statistically significant at 5% significance level compared to placebo

milestones.title: People receiving an incretin agonist reach ≥10% weight loss at 26 weeks in a phase 2 trial.
milestones.criterion: The prespecified secondary endpoint is the proportion of participants losing at least 10% of baseline body weight at 26 weeks in a randomized dose-ranging trial. NCT03131687 randomized 318 adults with type 2 diabetes; 316 received treatment. Frías et al. reported on 4 October 2018 that 6–39% of tirzepatide recipients across doses reached this endpoint, compared with 0% receiving placebo. The protocol specified no minimum responder proportion.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly, NCT03131687, secondary endpoint reported by Frías et al.; written for adults with type 2 diabetes.
milestones.threshold_quote: proportion of patients with at least 5% and 10% bodyweight loss from baseline to 26 weeks.

milestones.title: A phase 3 incretin trial beats placebo for ≥20% weight-loss responses at 72 weeks.
milestones.criterion: SURMOUNT-1's prespecified key secondary test compares tirzepatide 10 mg or 15 mg with placebo for the proportion losing ≥20% of baseline body weight at 72 weeks, with control of type I error. Among 2,539 randomized adults without diabetes, the estimated proportions were 50% with 10 mg (n=636), 57% with 15 mg (n=630), and 3% with placebo (n=643); both comparisons had P<0.001. The coprimary mean-weight-change and ≥5% response endpoints also met superiority tests. Results were published on 4 June 2022.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly, SURMOUNT-1 protocol NCT04184622, described in the SURMOUNT programme design paper; written for adults without diabetes.
milestones.threshold_quote: Key secondary end points include the proportion of participants achieving a body weight reduction ≥10%, ≥15%, or ≥20%

not_found: Coskun et al.'s supplementary DOCX could not be read, leaving the preclinical mouse group sizes unverified.
The full text of the phase 2 Lancet paper was blocked; its endpoints and results were available in the opened PubMed abstract.

results.finding: LY3298176 reduced body weight versus vehicle in diet-induced obese mice; sample size not stated; P<0.05.
results.detail: Chronic treatment also produced greater weight loss than semaglutide. Starting weight was about 45 g. The figure caption specifies one-way repeated-measures ANOVA, while the methods describe two-way repeated-measures ANOVA for chronic studies.
results.quote:
For body weight and food consumption differences,
P < 0.05
using one-way ANOVA repeated measures versus the vehicle (*) or semaglutide (+) treated groups.

results.finding: In 53 participants with type 2 diabetes, LY3298176 titrated to 10 mg reduced body weight versus placebo by 2.62 kg at day 29.
results.detail: The 95% CI for the placebo-adjusted difference was −3.79 to −1.45 kg. Body weight was a secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures.
results.quote: doses of 10 mg and 15 mg had a relevant effect in T2DM patients (LSM difference [95% CI]: −2.62 kg [−3.79, −1.45] and −2.07 kg [−3.25, −0.88], respectively.

results.finding: In a phase 2 trial of 316 treated adults with type 2 diabetes, 6–39% receiving LY3298176 achieved at least 10% weight loss at 26 weeks.
results.detail: The secondary endpoint was assessed in the modified intention-to-treat on-treatment dataset; 0% of placebo recipients reached it.
results.quote: At 26 weeks, 14-71% of those treated with LY3298176 achieved the weight loss target of at least 5% (vs 22% with dulaglutide, 0% with placebo) and 6-39% achieved the weight loss target of at least 10% (vs 9% with dulaglutide, 0% with placebo).

results.finding: In Study 1, 56.7% of 630 adults assigned tirzepatide 15 mg lost at least 20% of body weight at 72 weeks.
results.detail: The corresponding placebo response was 3.1% among 643 participants. The label reports greater responses with tirzepatide, but the supplied text does not establish the prespecified type I error control, P values, or 4 June 2022 publication date required by the criterion.
